title: Descent of an ample line bundle through a finite-branch quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $X,Y$ be proper $S$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $a:X\to Y$ be a finite surjective $S$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Let $T\hookrightarrow Y$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and put $Z=X\times_YT$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume that $|Z|$ is finite and that $a$ induces an isomorphism $X\setminus Z\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\setminus T$. Let $L$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open containing $Z$. Then there exist an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq Y$ of $T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], a trivialization of $L|_{a^{-1}W}$, and an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $M$ with $M|_W\cong\mathcal O_W$ and $a^*M\cong L$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; on $Y\setminus T$, $M$ identifies with $L|_{X\setminus Z}$ through the given isomorphism. The sheaf $M$ is ample. There are an integer $n\geq0$ and a closed $S$-immersion $Y\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};S)$; in particular $Y/S$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention [def-kun-projective]. Empty $Z,T$, nonclosed points of $Z$, and nonnormal or disconnected schemes are allowed. No flatness of $a$, existence of a group action, or etale branch assumption is imposed.

source.place: Agent extraction of old steps 6--8: Tag 0F20 (lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section); explicit two-open module gluing in sheaves.tex (lemma-glue-sheaves and lemma-glue-sheaves-structures); coherent.tex Tag 0B5V (lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample); ample immersion and proper monomorphism closed-immersion arguments as cited in the retained report.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-affine-invertible-finite-set-section to the affine scheme $U$, the restriction $L|_U$, and the finite subset $|Z|$. Obtain $s\in\Gamma(U,L|_U)$ nonzero in every residue-field fibre over $|Z|$. By lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes, $V=U_s$ is open and $s$ gives an isomorphism $\tau:\mathcal O_V\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_V$. Thus $|Z|\subseteq V\subseteq U$. Restriction preserves the local rank-one presentations of $L$, so the section lemma applies. Neither lemma requires the points of $Z$ to be closed.

Put $C=|X|\setminus V$. Since $a$ is finite, lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres says $a(C)$ is closed. Set $W=Y\setminus a(C)$. For $t\in|T|$, every point above $t$ belongs to $|Z|=a^{-1}(|T|)\subseteq V$, hence $t\notin a(C)$. Therefore $|T|\subseteq W$. Also $a^{-1}W\subseteq V$ directly from the definition of $W$. Restrict $\tau$ to get $\tau_W:\mathcal O_{a^{-1}W}\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_{a^{-1}W}$.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper); closed-image shrinking as in divisors.tex Tag 0BUT (lemma-finite-trivialize-invertible-upstairs).

proof.text: Let $D=Y\setminus T$, $E=X\setminus Z$, and let $b:E\xrightarrow{\sim}D$ be the given isomorphism. Transport $L|_E$ along $b$ to an invertible module $N$ on $D$. The two opens $W,D$ cover $Y$. On $W\cap D$, the inverse image under $b$ lies in $a^{-1}W$, so $\tau_W$ transports to an isomorphism $\alpha:\mathcal O_{W\cap D}\xrightarrow{\sim}N|_{W\cap D}$. Use $\alpha$ for the transition from $\mathcal O_W$ to $N$, $\alpha^{-1}$ for the reverse transition, and identities on equal indices. All cocycle equalities reduce to $\alpha^{-1}\alpha=1$ or $\alpha\alpha^{-1}=1$. Clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules gives a module $M$ with charts $c_W:M|_W\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_W$ and $c_D:M|_D\xrightarrow{\sim}N$, satisfying $c_D=\alpha c_W$ on the overlap. These charts make $M$ locally free of rank one, hence invertible in the sense of def-sc-invertible-module. They give the asserted identifications on $W$ and $D$.

source.place: Tags 00AL (lemma-glue-sheaves) and 00AM (lemma-glue-sheaves-structures), applied to a two-open cover.

proof.text: We verify $a^*M\cong L$ with the actual transition maps. By pullback functoriality and the identification of open-immersion pullback with restriction, $c_W$ gives on $a^{-1}W$ the map $a^*M\to\mathcal O_{a^{-1}W}\xrightarrow{\tau_W}L$; here the pullback of $\mathcal O_W$ is $\mathcal O_{a^{-1}W}$ by the tensor unit formula in def-pc-module-pullback. On $E$, pulling back $c_D$ along $b$ gives $a^*M|_E\xrightarrow{\sim}b^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_E$. On $E\cap a^{-1}W$, the equality $c_D=\alpha c_W$ and the definition of $\alpha$ show that both maps send a local section to the same multiple of $s$. Thus they agree. Clause (1) of lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules glues these maps on the open cover $X=a^{-1}W\cup E$. Their inverse local maps agree as well, and glue to an inverse by the same clause; their two composites are identities by uniqueness of gluing. This proves the claimed global isomorphism.

The isomorphism $a^*M\cong L$ and lem-sc-ample-iso imply that $a^*M$ is ample. Apply lem-trf-finite-surjective-ample-reflection with its source $Y$ equal to our $X$, its target $X$ equal to our $Y$, its morphism $f=a$, and its line bundle $\mathcal L=M$. Its hypotheses are precisely the Noetherian ring $R$, properness of both schemes over $R$, finiteness and surjectivity of $a$, and invertibility of $M$, all already given or proved. It follows that $M$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 0B5V (lemma-surjective-finite-morphism-ample); properties.tex Definition 01PS for invariance under module isomorphism.

proof.text: Properness of $Y\to S$ includes finite type, hence local finite type. Apply lem-weil-pbc-ample-very-ample-immersion-affine-base with $A=R$, $X=Y$, and $\mathcal L=M$. Since $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ is affine, this gives an integer $n\geq0$ and an $S$-immersion $i:Y\to P_n=\operatorname{Proj}(R[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$. Here $q_n:P_n\to S$ is the structure morphism specified by that lemma; the comparison of $P_n$ with $\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};S)$ is made in step 7.

By lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated, $P_n\to S$ is separated. Since $Y\to S$ is proper, lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target makes $i$ proper. The proper immersion lemma lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed now makes $i$ a closed immersion. Apply lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension with its ring map $\mathbf Z\to R$, its graded ring $A=\mathbf Z[T_0,\ldots,T_n]$, $B=R[x_0,\ldots,x_n]$ and $\beta:R\otimes_{\mathbf Z}A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$, $r\otimes T_k\mapsto rx_k$: the square formed by $P_n\to\operatorname{Proj}A$, $q_n=p_B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is cartesian, so there is an isomorphism $\theta:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};S)=S\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Proj}A$ with first projection $\circ\,\theta=q_n$. Then $\theta\circ i$ is a closed immersion over $S$. Together with $n\geq0$, this is exactly projectivity in def-kun-projective. If $Z$ is empty, surjectivity of $a$ forces $T$ empty; the section and shrinking construction still works (one may take $V=W=\varnothing$), and gluing is then just transport through $X\cong Y$. Empty schemes and disconnected or nonnormal schemes require no change to any argument.
